items.title: 750 Mississauga aerospace workers are joining Bombardier in major local takeover
items.summary: A major aerospace operation in Mississauga is about to change ownership, with approximately 750 local workers set to become Bombardier employees. , better known as MHICA, from its parent company, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI). The deal is expected to close later this year, subject to regulatory approvals and other closing conditions. For Mississauga, the agreement means a long-established aerospace operation near Pearson Airport will become part of Bombardier’s existing manufacturing operation in the city. And for the approximately 750 people who work at MHICA, Bombardier says the transition is intended to be business as usual. Mitsubishi Heavy Industries is a major Japanese industrial company with businesses ranging from energy and infrastructure to aerospace and defence. MHI Canada Aerospace is its Canadian aerospace operation. The company was incorporated in Ontario in 2006 and has operated in Mississauga for nearly two decades. MHICA’s main facility is at 6390 Northwest Drive in the Malton area, where it operates a large manufacturing plant and logistics centre. The company currently lists 725 employees at the location.

items.title: Tow truck driver faces more serious charge after pedestrian struck in Mississauga dies
items.summary: A Mississauga tow truck driver charged in a collision involving a pedestrian late last year in the city’s east end now faces a more serious charge after the man who was struck died in hospital, police say. Peel Regional Police Major Collision Bureau investigators looking into the Tuesday, Dec. 16, 2025 incident said the 45-year-old man who was hit by the tow truck succumbed to his injuries in hospital some seven months later, on July 29. , according to police. Investigators said at the time the man was rushed to a local trauma centre with life-threatening injuries. Following the man’s death this summer, investigators upgraded the charge against the tow truck driver. Abner Zuniga, 49, of Mississauga, was charged back in March with dangerous operation of a vehicle causing bodily harm in relation to the December 2025 collision. That charge has now been upgraded to dangerous operation of a vehicle causing death, police said in a news release issued on Wednesday. The investigation remains ongoing and anyone with information is asked to contact Peel Regional Police Major Collision Bureau investigators at 905-453-2121, ext. 3710.

items.title: Pedestrian Succumbs to Injuries Following 2025 Collision in Mississauga
items.summary: Region of Peel – Investigators from the Major Collision Bureau (MCB) have upgraded charges against a tow truck driver after a pedestrian involved in a collision last year has died from his injuries. , a 45-year-old male pedestrian was struck by a tow truck while crossing Rathburn Road East near Dixie Road in Mississauga. The pedestrian suffered life-threatening injuries and was transported to a local trauma centre. On March 24, 2026, Abner Zuniga, a 49-year-old Mississauga man, was charged with Dangerous Operation Causing Bodily Harm in relation to the collision. On July 29, 2026, the victim succumbed to his injuries in hospital. As a result, the accused’s charges were upgraded to Dangerous Operation Causing Death. The investigation remains ongoing. items.title: Fighter jets, other aircraft take to skies over Toronto and Mississauga
items.summary: As usual this time of year, the skies above Mississauga and Toronto — and other parts of the GTA — will again serve as a backdrop in the coming days for numerous aircraft not often seen in this airspace. In addition, Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga and, to a lesser degree, Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport are again serving as home bases to the many jets taking part in the annual Canadian International Air Show over Labour Day weekend at the CNE in Toronto. Featuring performers that include the beloved Canadian Forces Snowbirds (see video below), who’ll be pausing operations after 2026, in addition to Canada’s CF-18 demonstration team, an RCMP Black Hawk Helicopter and many more, Canada’s largest and longest-running air show is once again expected to “wow” those who gather by the lake in Toronto to watch the aerial action. The show, in its 77th year and enjoyed by masses of people annually on the shores of Lake Ontario, is also North America’s longest-running air show, organizers point out. m. each day. m. The numerous planes taking part in the main event are, as always, stationed at Toronto Pearson Airport and Billy Bishop while in town this week through Monday. The aircraft will “transport from those airports to the show site,” air show organizers said earlier, adding that “at times they may be flying over” both Toronto and Mississauga. Leading up to and during the annual aviation spectacle, the airspace over the country’s seventh-largest city is at times dotted with any number of Canadian and American fighter jets impressively streaking across the sky as they tune up for the big event.

items.title: Ridgeway Plaza Dessert Shops Get a Boost After Viral Food Influencer's Mississauga Stop
items.summary: According to INsauga, food influencer Jordan Howlett, known online as Jordan the Stallion, recently stopped by Ridgeway Plaza in Mississauga and sampled desserts at two local businesses. The outlet reports Howlett tried the cookie dough and ice cream at Nora Cakes & Sweets before heading to The Dough Diaries to sample its Original Pudding Cake. INsauga reports Howlett has built a massive following on TikTok and Instagram that now numbers in the tens of millions, built in part on his humorous food commentary and his Fast Food Secrets Club series. According to the outlet, he is also known for his trademark bathroom mirror introductions and his now famous Come here catchphrase. INsauga reports the exposure could be significant for the two dessert businesses, since Howlett's audience skews young and heavily toward food enthusiasts.

items.title: Rare Topps Baseball Card Puts Mississauga's Name Ahead of Josh Naylor's Own
items.summary: According to INsauga, Seattle Mariners first baseman Josh Naylor has been given the nickname Mississauga Masher on a rare variation card in the 2026 Topps Heritage set. The outlet reports the design, which pays tribute to the classic 1977 Topps look, replaces Naylor's name with the nickname, a rare touch for a city with little history of appearing on major-league baseball cards. INsauga reports the card is one of only 10 Nickname Variations included in the set, alongside players such as Bobby Witt Jr., nicknamed Bobby Baseball, Kyle Schwarber as Schwarbs, Cal Raleigh as Big Dumper and Roman Anthony as Roman Empire. According to the outlet, Naylor's card is numbered 129 in the set and is a short print, meaning it is considerably harder for collectors to find than the standard version. INsauga reports the card adds a bit of novelty for a city not typically associated with major-league baseball memorabilia.

items.title: Peel Region Cities Rank Among Canada's Best for Investment After Adding Over 5,000 Jobs
items.summary: According to INsauga, a new report credits major investment projects with creating more than 5,000 new jobs across Mississauga and Brampton over the past year. The outlet reports the figure includes nearly 4,000 new jobs in Mississauga and 1,265 in Brampton, with both cities again ranking highly on Site Selection magazine's annual list of the best Canadian municipalities for investment. INsauga reports notable Mississauga projects included a corporate headquarters expansion worth $127 million that added 136 jobs, along with a $13 million Citigroup expansion that created 600 jobs. According to the outlet, Brampton's gains came from projects including the $141 million expansion of the Coca-Cola Canada Bottling Plant, a new Mobile Climate Control manufacturing and research facility adding 700 jobs, and a fourth advanced manufacturing facility from Powersmiths adding 200 jobs. INsauga reports Ontario ranked first among Canadian provinces for investment in the report, ahead of Alberta and Saskatchewan, with the report crediting the province's business case as remaining strong despite trade friction with the United States.

items.title: Niagara Region Drug Raids Send 30-Year-Old Mississauga Man to Court on Multiple Charges
items.summary: According to INsauga, a Mississauga man is facing charges after Niagara Regional Police executed search warrants tied to a cocaine trafficking investigation near Niagara Falls. The outlet reports the investigation began in July when detectives started looking into the suspected sale of cocaine by a man in St. Catharines. INsauga reports street crime unit officers carried out two search warrants on Tuesday in Welland and Thorold, recovering more than $100,000 in suspected cocaine along with nearly $50,000 in cash. According to the outlet, the raids led to the arrests of Ismail Ahmed, 30, of Mississauga, and Chantal Fournier, 35, of Welland. INsauga reports Ahmed remains in custody with a bail hearing scheduled for Wednesday in St. Catharines court, while Fournier was released with a future court date yet to be set on a charge of possession of proceeds of property obtained by crime over $5,000.

items.title: Mississauga Bylaw Officers to Patrol for Illegal Fireworks Through the Labour Day Weekend
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, backyard fireworks displays are not allowed anywhere in the city this Labour Day long weekend, including the holiday Monday, unless residents first obtain a permit. The city reports fireworks without a permit are only permitted on Victoria Day, Canada Day, Diwali, Lunar New Year and New Year's Eve, and officials have suggested residents celebrate instead with glow sticks, noisemakers or sparklers. According to the city, bylaw enforcement officers will be out in full force over the long weekend to make sure fireworks are not being sold or used illegally. The city says residents can report illegal fireworks use or ask general questions by searching fireworks on the city's website or calling the 311 information line. According to the city, Mississauga logged 58 fireworks complaints during this year's Canada Day period, running from June 26 to July 2, down slightly from 63 complaints during the same period in 2025, when 221 vendor inspections led to two charges for non-permitted sales.

items.title: Donald Kent Obituary | Turner & Porter Funeral Directors Ltd. | Mississauga, ON
items.summary: 4 Trees, Flowers, or Condolences have been sent in support of Donald’s family — View on Tribute Wall 4 Trees, Flowers, or Condolences have been sent in support of Donald’s family — View on Tribute Wall Passed away peacefully on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, at the age of 87. Beloved husband of his late wife, Ursula, for 58 years. Don was a man of steadfast faith, drawing strength and comfort from his beliefs throughout his life. He was a kind and hardworking man, generous with his time and always ready to lend a helping hand. In the later years of his life, he devoted himself to the care of his wife. He cared for her with quiet strength and compassion through the long journey of her progressive illness. His selflessness was a testament to the depth of his character. He will be deeply missed and forever cherished, living on in the hearts and memories of all who knew and loved him. Don is survived by his three children, Glenn (Christine), Lisa (Michael) and Kimberley (Anthony). Proud grandpa to Anthony, Luca and Adrian. Dear brother-in-law to Carol, Fay, Desales and Loyola, and uncle to many nieces and nephews. Predeceased by his parents, Patrick and Mary Kent; siblings Gordon (Catherine), Bob (Kate), Myles, Marguerite (Doug) and Joan (Lynn); and siblings-in-law Lucy (Peter), Denise (Ronald), Bill, Michael and Anne.

items.title: $35,000 in Stolen Merchandise Recovered as Mississauga Man Faces Dozens of Theft Charges
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Peel police say a 49-year-old Mississauga man has been charged with more than three dozen offences after a two-month investigation into a suspected prolific retail thief. The outlet reports the investigation, dubbed Project Bishop, began in April after officers identified a suspect believed to be behind numerous thefts of clothing and accessories from major retailers. Mississauga.com reports police linked the man to at least 38 theft-related incidents across Peel, Halton, Durham, York and Niagara regions, with the value of stolen merchandise in each incident ranging from about $50 to more than $4,000. According to the outlet, the man was arrested on June 19 and charged with 24 counts of theft under $5,000 and 14 counts of possession of property obtained by crime. Mississauga.com reports that following the arrest, search warrants executed at homes in Mississauga and Welland turned up more than $35,000 worth of stolen merchandise, including clothing, cosmetics and personal accessories.
